Paragraph:
Translation: Work done as a sacrifice for Visnu has to be performed, otherwise work binds one to this material world. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your prescribed duties for His satisfaction, and in that way you will always remain unattached and free from bondage.

Purport (Excerpt): ...Any other work done in this material world will be a cause of bondage, for both good and evil work have their reactions... Therefore, one has to work in Krsna consciousness to satisfy Krsna... Nothing should be performed for sense gratification, but everything should be done for the satisfaction of Krsna...
Situation/Problem_Faced: How to act in the world without incurring psychological burdens, anxiety, and karmic entanglement.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna reveals the secret of unattached action: work must be performed as a sacrifice (Yajna) for the Supreme. When work is dedicated to a higher transcendent purpose rather than ego gratification, it creates no psychological bondage.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is given the key formula to participate in action (warfare) without being psychologically burdened by its consequences.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purpose-Driven Action: Reframing work as a contribution to a higher purpose (Yajna)
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Detachment from Outcomes: Focusing entirely on performance of duty rather than egoic reward
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Freedom from Karma/Burden: Avoiding the mental weight of expectation and regret

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Yajnarthat karma (Work performed strictly as a sacrifice to Visnu)
Karma-bandhana (Entanglement or bondage resulting from selfish actions)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Work performed for personal gratification binds the soul to karmic consequences. However, when work is executed as a dedicated sacrifice (Yajna) for Lord Visnu, it becomes a liberating process that frees the practitioner from all material attachment and karma.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Selfish, ego-driven goals create chronic anxiety because we tie our self-worth to specific outcomes. Reframing your daily labor as a selfless contribution or service to a higher purpose releases you from the fear of failure and outcome-obsession, allowing you to work with focus and peace.
